messages:
ashley: Heads-up — want to kick off a short thread about simplifying console query contracts to reduce fanout and RBAC checks. Observed tail latency spikes on dashboards when tenant count grows.

sam-pl: +1. Do we have perf numbers? https://grafana.redwood.local/d/dash/perf-overview

maria-eng-platform: Quick summary: dashboards do N parallel queries per widget, each query runs authz check across row-level perms. At ~500 tenants that becomes 3–5x latency and lots of small DB queries.

raj-sre: We saw p99 go from ~180ms -> ~1.2s on heavy dashboards this morning, correlated with authz DB CPU and connection churn.

ashley: Proposed refactor: push authz filtering earlier into the projection layer and merge per-tenant checks, plus introduce an optional "compact route" that returns pre-filtered projections for common query signatures.

katie: Is that the same as the tiling/cache idea from last year? We should avoid tile explosion and invalidation complexity.

maria-eng-platform: Not tiles — more like a projection-side index: for a given dashboard query signature we materialize a tenant->allowed-ids map and cache it for 60s. That reduces N auth DB hits to 1 and lets the query engine apply a single filter pass.

sam-pl: Tradeoffs: extra memory footprint per signature, eventual consistency window, and complexity in invalidation when perms change. Also increased code surface in the query layer.

ashley: Invalidation story: on role/perm changes we emit an event to the invalidation topic. Consumers can lazily refresh on next request or force-evict. Worst-case TTL is 60s during rollout.

maria-eng-platform: Implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
query_engine.handle(req) {
  key = signature(req) 
  allowed = projection_cache.get_or_compute(key, tenant=req.tenant_id, ttl=60s, computeFn=() -> authz.lookup_batch(...))
  return base_query.filter(ids=allowed)
}
```

leo: How does this interact with dedicated customer isolation? We must ensure strict namespacing to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

maria-eng-platform: We'll namespace cache keys with tenant id and server-side sign the entries. Data stays in-process or in tenant-scoped redis; no cross-tenant keys.

raj-sre: Load test plan: run a 10k dashboard fanout sim with perms churn every 30s, measure p50/p95/p99 and DB QPS. Watch for cache storms and eviction thundering.

sam-pl: UX for operators: add an admin console endpoint to purge cache for a tenant + emit audit log event. Also expose miss rate and hit latency metrics.

ashley: Agree. Document the interface boundary: projection-cache API must accept `signature`, `tenant_id`, `force_refresh` and return `list_of_ids` + `version_token`. Keep deterministic signatures to avoid cache duplication.

katie: One more safety: keep an opt-in fallback path that uses original per-widget authz if compact route fails or indicates suspicious data. Roll forwards with feature flag per tenant.

maria-eng-platform: Rollout plan: canary 5% tenants -> 25% -> 100% using FF gating. Telemetry: measure miss rate, latencies, DB QPS, and correctness (compare result sets on canary).

ashley: OK. Can someone draft a short RFC with diagrams and riskiest assumptions called out? Target: 2-week spike + 1-week rollout plan.

sam-pl: I'll draft the RFC today and add perf numbers from the morning run.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag-lib v1.3 -> staging :rocket:

ashley: thanks. tagging @maria-eng-platform @sam-pl @raj-sre for followups :thumbsup:
